#select
    We can select(A,B) or select(A:D) --> which select A,B,C,D
    We can also use select(starts_with("xxx")), then replace xxx into the letter ot the word that we want to select.
    We can also exclude things using select: select(!species) is gonna exclude column"species".
        We can also intergate select(!contains("x")) into it. Then we will select colums that have x in it.


```{r}
penguins |> select(starts_with("b") | starts_with("f")) 
```

#The distinct function will remove rows that have the same value for a selected criteria.

#1
```{r}
penguins |> distinct(species,island) |> head()
```

#2
```{r}
penguins |> filter(body_mass > 4000) |> distinct(sex)
```

#3
```{r}
penguins |> filter(species == "Gentoo" & island == "Biscoe") |> distinct(year)
```

# Inside one funciton, we can add different selection helplers, but inside one selection helplers, we can not have multiple criteria. 
eg. select(starts_with("b"|"f")) --> select(stars_with("b") | select(starts_with("f")))

# mutate()
mutate() create a new column based on certain given calculation
e.g. mutate(abcde = a / b). 
*when there are a lot of command, it is better to create new line like L113-L117

#1
```{r}
penguins |> 
    mutate(body_mass_kg = body_mass / 1000)
```

#2
```{r}
penguins |> 
    mutate(flipper_to_mass_ratio = flipper_len / body_mass) |> 
    arrange(desc(flipper_to_mass_ratio))
```

#3
```{r}
penguins |> 
    mutate(heavy = body_mass > 4500)
```
